note: Maritime policy and programme evolution dataset. Proposals, budget announcements, approved schemes, guidelines and operational programmes are kept distinct — a proposal is never labelled approved without a captured Cabinet/authority decision. Each record carries the issuing authority, announcement date, formal approval date where applicable, status, objectives and funding.

policies.name: National Waterways Act, 2016
policies.objectives: Declared 111 national waterways (5 existing + 106 new) totalling 20,187 km, making waterway development a statutory national mandate; IWAI (IWAI Act 1985) is the development agency. 32 waterways operational as of March 2026.

policies.name: Major Port Authorities Act, 2021
policies.objectives: Replaced the Major Port Trusts Act 1963; converted 11 of the 12 major ports into port authorities with empowered boards (Kamarajar Port remains a government-owned company).

policies.name: Maritime India Vision 2030
policies.objectives: 150+ initiatives across 10 themes: port capacity to ~1,958 MMT at major ports, container turnaround under 20 hours, berth output above 30,000 tonnes, transshipment share, shipbuilding, Sagarmanthan portal, ViBhaS/NAVIC cells.
policies.funding: Investment of the order of ₹3-3.5 lakh crore.

policies.name: Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
policies.objectives: 300+ initiatives across 11 themes: port capacity 10,000+ MMTPA, 3 transshipment hubs, 2 new major ports, Top-10 shipbuilding nation by 2030 / Top-5 by 2047, world's leading ship-recycling destination, waterways cargo >500 MMTPA, 175 million TEU containers (base case).
policies.funding: Investment pipeline of ~₹80 lakh crore; ~₹23,000 crore of projects inaugurated at launch; 300+ MoUs worth ~₹7 lakh crore.

policies.name: Sagar Aankalan (Logistics Port Performance Index)
policies.objectives: National port-performance index guidelines benchmarking port and terminal efficiency by cargo category; FY 2024-25 edition ranked 12 major and 35 non-major terminals (container category led by Mundra, JNPA second).

policies.name: Jalvahak long-haul inland-waterway incentive
policies.objectives: 35% cargo incentive for long-haul movement on national waterways to shift freight from road to water; budget head ₹30 crore in 2026-27.

policies.name: Sagarmala Startup & Innovation Initiative (S2I2)
policies.objectives: Startup and innovation pipeline for Sagarmala 2.0: Maritime Innovation Fund as anchor vehicle, Maritime Innovation Hubs at IIT Madras, Bombay, Kharagpur and IMU, MAR-a-THON 2025 hackathon.
policies.funding: Anchored in the Maritime Innovation Fund.

policies.name: Sagarmala Finance Corporation Ltd (restructuring of SDCL)
policies.objectives: India's first maritime-focused NBFC; inaugurated 26 June 2025; ~₹4,300 crore of loan approvals by December 2025.
policies.funding: Restructured from SDCL (₹1,000 crore authorised capital).

policies.name: National Shipbuilding and Ship Repair Policy package (₹69,725 crore)
policies.objectives: Four-pillar approach: Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) ₹24,736 crore to 31 March 2036 including a ₹4,001 crore shipbreaking credit note; Maritime Development Fund ₹25,000 crore (MIF ₹20,000 crore + IIF ₹5,000 crore); Shipbuilding Dock Support ₹19,989 crore; targets 4.5 million GT additional capacity and ~30 lakh jobs.

policies.name: Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme
policies.authority: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways / Ministry of Finance
policies.objectives: Raise coastal shipping's freight modal share from 6% to 12% by 2047; announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 speech.

policies.name: Container Manufacturing Scheme
policies.objectives: ₹10,000 crore scheme to build domestic container manufacturing capacity, reducing dependence on imported containers for EXIM trade.

policies.name: 20 new national waterways (starting NW-5)
policies.objectives: Development of 20 new national waterways, starting with NW-5 (Talcher–Paradip/Dhamra) connecting Odisha's mineral belt to the coast; ship-repair clusters at Varanasi and Patna.

policies.name: Sagarmala 2.0
policies.status_note: No Cabinet approval captured in any primary source on file. An earlier ₹40,000 crore budgetary-support figure (March 2025) was superseded by the ₹85,482 crore figure in the April 2026 backgrounder; both retained as dated observations.
policies.objectives: Proposed successor phase with total budgetary support of ₹85,482 crore and total investment of ₹3.6 lakh crore; preparation anchored by S2I2 and the Maritime Innovation Fund.
policies.funding: ₹85,482 crore budgetary support; ₹3.6 lakh crore total investment (proposed).

policies.name: Union Budget 2026-27 — MoPSW allocation
policies.objectives: Demand No. 78 (MoPSW) BE ₹5,164.80 crore: Sagarmala head ₹616.88 crore, SBFAS/NSM ₹515 crore, SbDS ₹250 crore, MDF ₹1,000 crore, Jalvahak ₹30 crore.
